lead: Anthropic (ANT), the biggest IPO ever ($81.3B raised at $83), opened at $111.50 (+34.3%) and closed at $97.17 (+17.1%), but its biggest outside owners fell: Amazon -3.87% to $257.37 and Alphabet -3.46% (GOOGL $272.66) as the S&P 500 dropped 2.02% for a sixth straight loss.
why: Profit-taking in the 'Anthropic proxies': CNBC (via Stock Titan) said Amazon, Alphabet and Broadcom are broadly seen as proxies for Anthropic and investors appeared to take profits once it began trading; the debut 'failed to revive enthusiasm' for AI stocks.
Rates: traders priced a near-certain 25 bp Fed hike in December (Reuters, LSEG data); 10-year ~5.05%, VIX ~28; Philly Fed fell to 6.3 from 20.9. Dow -1,101 (-2.19%), Nasdaq -2.25%.

Anthropic itself: $15B bought in the first minute; 30 minutes in, no big US IPO since 2008 was further below its first trade (Yahoo). Stakes at $83: Amazon ~$159B, Alphabet ~$149B (Forbes); Fool puts Alphabet's at ~$175B at the close. Also: AMD -7.7% on a China blacklist report, Intuit -14.6% after hours on Q1 and a Mailchimp sale, Palo Alto +6.4%.
